newsitem.title: UK: Iraq not telling full truth about weapons - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Iraq not telling full truth about weapons - U.N.

text.p: The head of the latest United Nations inspection team to visit Iraq said on Thursday his group found evidence that Baghdad had still not disclosed the full extent of its secret weapons programme.

"I found evidence of a biological weapons programme which had not been revealed to us," Colonel Terry Taylor told reporters. He said the Iraqis had briefly mentioned the programme to the U.N. team but had not revealed how advanced it was.
Taylor said the weapon was a toxin agent, but would not disclose more details of exactly what his 21-strong team had discovered. The inspection team was in Iraq from April 5 to 20.
"The Iraqis had briefly mentioned the programme to us, but what was new was the extent of the work which had been done on it," he said.

Rolf Ekeus, head of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, accused Baghdad earlier this month of concealing a small but significant quantity of banned weapons. Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz denied the charge on Wednesday.

"Aziz is not telling the truth when he says the Iraqis have revealed everything," said Taylor, who made his comments during a briefing held by the International Institute for Strategic Studies think-tank.
